name: Kuala Lumpur
tagline: Twin towers, temple steps and food streets
summary: Combine KLCC with Bukit Bintang and keep the heritage core for another walk. Batu Caves is a separate northern excursion rather than a quick stop between central attractions.
seasonNote: Hot and humid throughout the year; heavy showers are common, so keep indoor alternatives.
arrival: KLIA Ekspres reaches KL Sentral; buses cost less and taxis can suit groups.
gettingAround: Use MRT/LRT and a booked car where stations are inconvenient; walking connections vary.
cashTip: Carry ringgit for food stalls and markets; established malls accept cards widely.
foodTip: Try nasi lemak, roti canai and noodles; halal options are extensive but individual stalls vary.
buyTip: Central Market is convenient for crafts and batik; compare quality and country of manufacture.
baseArea: Bukit Bintang for food or KLCC for skyline access.

connections.note: Airborne time only; door-to-door rail/coach choices differ substantially.
Flight to Denpasar followed by a slow Ubud road transfer.

whyVisit: The city’s most recognisable towers with a timed skybridge visit.

items.name: Dewakan
items.summary: Chef Darren Teoh’s two-star Malaysian tasting menu, served 48 floors up with views across Kuala Lumpur.
items.expect: A long tasting-menu meal. Deposits, cancellation fees and smart-casual dress codes are common at this level.
items.tip: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.

whyVisit: Chef Darren Teoh’s two-star Malaysian tasting menu, served 48 floors up with views across Kuala Lumpur.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Two MICHELIN Stars (excellent cooking), a rare level of recognition.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.
